anti_overlap: Focus on the choice of levels and the pick rule's structure, not on trace plumbing
decision_lens: Is {5, 10, 20} a well-chosen trio — does 10 sit at a genuinely distinctive structural position, or is it just arithmetically between two arbitrary endpoints? A good trio has the middle as an independent reference; a bad trio has a middle that merely interpolates.
distance_rationale: A West African oral-music craft with highly refined sensibilities about tuning references and nested intervals — the kora's nested-trio tuning is structurally isomorphic to three-point parameter calibration yet semantically remote from software testing.
expected_isomorphisms: The jali's concern that a middle reference string be independently audible (not dragged by its neighbors) maps to the requirement that the chosen budget reflect a structural property, not mere arithmetic centrality between endpoints.
focus: Evaluating the 5/10/20 three-level decision tree against the jali tradition of tuning the kora's 21 strings in nested trios, where three reference strings are picked precisely so the middle is audibly unbound by the others and the outer two define the usable register.
name: fd-gambian-jaliya-trio-tuning
persona: Apply the perspective of a Gambian jali (griot) master tuning a kora — they care about whether a three-string reference trio produces a middle tone that rings freely without being pulled by the outer strings, they measure by ear the decay time of the middle string after plucking, and they flag when the trio is chosen such that the middle ties to an outer string (beat frequencies, resonance coupling) making the 'middle pick' illusory. Here the 'trio' is {5, 10, 20} and the 'middle' is the default pick of 10.
review_areas: Whether the 5/10/20 spacing reflects a substantive hypothesis about the sim's attention-spend distribution or is chosen for convenience
Whether the 'demote to 5 only if 10 binds, promote to 20 only if both bind' asymmetry correctly encodes preference for parsimony

Whether the FAIL path (all three bind) has a defined widening strategy — is the next trio {10, 20, 40}? {2, 5, 10}? The brainstorm says 'escalate to user' but the jali tradition insists the next trio is pre-declared
Whether there is a single-level sanity probe at B=1 or B=100 to bracket the bind/non-bind transition and confirm 10 is not accidentally on a plateau
Whether the pick rule's behavior is symmetric around the middle — a trio that systematically resolves to the middle regardless of data is a rubber-stamp trio

severity_examples.condition: All three levels are on the same plateau; the trio does not distinguish — the 'pick medium' rule resolves trivially and the calibration provides no information
severity_examples.scenario: Null is non-binding at B=5 and B=10 and B=20 identically with remaining always equal to per_year

severity_examples.condition: Escalation to user is ad-hoc; reproducibility of the calibration protocol is broken
severity_examples.scenario: FAIL path triggers but no pre-declared widening trio exists

success_hints: Demand a single-point probe at an extreme (e.g., B=1) to show the trio actually straddles a transition
Pre-register the widening trio in PROTOCOL.md §7a so the FAIL path is deterministic
Check whether the sim's AttentionBudget default (10) coinciding with the trio middle creates a tautology — medium passes because medium is the historical default
task_context: The decision tree over 5/10/20 encodes the 'pick medium' preference. A jaliya-trio audit asks whether the trio is structurally informative and whether the pick rule is symmetric.
